A phone leaves the association list whil: A phone leaves the association list while it sleeps and reappears seconds later, so a sighting counts for this long. Below about a minute the states will flicker.
Appends every station the configured SNM: Appends every station the configured SNMP devices currently have associated, as inactive rows named after the address. The log lists them with their SSID and says which addresses are random ones, which is how a phone is told from a printer.
Community strings and SNMPv3 keys in thi: Community strings and SNMPv3 keys in this table are stored encrypted with the system secret. Anyone with access to the ioBroker host can still read them, so grant no more rights than the adapter needs.
Configure the device to send traps to th: Configure the device to send traps to this host under Services → SNMP → Trap Settings. Most Teltonika traps carry no values, so a trap is recorded and triggers an immediate poll of that device.
Devices without an MQTT publisher, such: Devices without an MQTT publisher, such as the TSW switches, can only be read over SNMP. Enable the SNMP agent on the device first.
Enter the MAC address the router shows u: Enter the MAC address the router shows under Status → Wireless, not the one printed on the phone: phones use a separate random address per network. It changes again when the network is forgotten and rejoined.
Every row is a person with one or more M: Every row is a person with one or more MAC addresses, separated by commas, and an optional group. The person gets its own branch under presence.persons with present, last arrival and departure, since when, the sums of the day and the last comings and goings; it is present while one of the routers reports one of its addresses as associated to Wi-Fi. Persons of one group are summarised under presence.groups. Read over SNMP only: the MQTT publisher of a router cannot report its clients.

Web user and password are only needed to: Web user and password are only needed to switch PoE, which SNMP cannot do. The adapter logs in to the Web API of the device over HTTPS and accepts its self-signed certificate.
